title: Certificación de distribución — CP2, CP4, CP5
scope_note: B6.W5 closes the distribution certification gate for the v0.101.16 release lane. The current HEAD is at v0.101.15 (workspace bump for v0.101.16 has not been committed yet, per the W6.B5 cierre pattern where the release bump is the last commit of a release cycle). The cert exercises every script and binary that would gate a v0.101.16 release at this SHA, and records honest NOT_RUN / SKIP_NOT_APPLICABLE for items that require a native runner, a signing key, or an artefact that does not yet exist on disk. Per PRF-DIST-05 (`docs/prf/specs/SPEC-DISTRIBUTION.md`), no platform is declared certified without a native build, a real UAT, and a published artefact that survives the lifecycle. CP6 (web / landing) is explicitly out of scope for B6.W5.

entries.result: no tool in product/tools.json declares an `install_instructions` field; the catalog does not advertise per-tool install paths yet. PRF-DIST-05 forbids announcing install paths without a real UAT, so the claim is honest NOT_RUN until the catalog is extended and the per-tool install instructions resolve to a published artefact.
entries.reason: The `install_instructions` field is not present on any tool in `product/tools.json` (catalog inspected at HEAD = e51f49ef). No per-tool install paths are advertised, so there is nothing to resolve to a published artefact. Adding the field is part of the B6.W3 lifecycle work; until then the contract is recorded as NOT_RUN rather than PASS.

entries.result: no v0.101.16 release artefacts on disk; `release/` only contains v0.101.10 tarballs and the SHA256SUMS / inventory for that release. A v0.101.16 candidate does not exist in this checkout, so the black-box install → doctor → CLI → MCP → update → rollback → uninstall smoke cannot be exercised against real artefacts.
entries.reason: v0.101.16 has not been released yet; the most recent release on disk is v0.101.10 (cogh / cognicode / cognicode-mcp / bundle / release-inventory tarballs). PRF-DIST-02 requires the smoke to run against real artefacts from a clean HOME/XDG, and there are no v0.101.16 artefacts to point it at. The smoke will run as part of the release-pipeline stage that produces v0.101.16; the cert entry will move to PASS at the same SHA.

entries.result: the smoke script exists at the documented path; mode 644 (no executable bit, but invokable via `bash` — the same convention `cargo test` uses for `*.sh` fixtures). The script's mandatory behaviour is recorded in the comments at the top of `release-install-smoke.sh` (publish-vs-target isolation, the 70 MB self-trash incident measured 2026-10-04, etc.).
entries.reason: The script's executable-bit absence is deliberate: the script is invoked through `bash scripts/ci/release-install-smoke.sh ...` from the release lane, never directly. Verifying it is invokable through `bash` is sufficient for this entry, which closes on 'the script that runs the install UAT is on disk at the path the lane expects'.

entries.result: `product/platforms.json` declares `linux-x86-64` and `linux-aarch64` as `support_level: "certified"`. PRF-DIST-05 contradicts this declaration: it requires build + native-runner execution + corpus + real UAT before a platform is certified. The catalogue-level claim and the contract-level claim are at odds; the contract wins until the catalogue is reconciled. linux-x86-64-musl is `experimental` (smoke build only); macos-arm64, macos-x86-64, windows-x86-64 are `unsupported`.
entries.reason: PRF-DIST-05 supersedes the support_level field. This entry records that the catalogue is more optimistic than the contract allows; the contract is the source of truth. The platforms.json field will be reconciled to `experimental` (or removed) in the same commit that lands the corresponding build/UAT for the platform. Until then no platform is advertised as certified.

entries.result: the attestation script exists, parses its arguments, dispatches to the help-text path, and exits 0 with the documented ADR excerpt printed on stdout. The exit-0 path exercises the entire argument parser, the `set -uo pipefail` policy, the missing-key guard, and the help-text dispatch.
entries.reason: Closing the script-exists + script-runs-in-help-mode claim on the actual observed exit code (0). The argument-parser contract is documented in `scripts/ci/attest-provenance.sh` lines 1-57; the --help path makes every public chunk the consumer can invoke non-destructively.

entries.result: the actual attestation against a v0.101.16 artefact is not run in this environment. The script requires a long-lived cosign signing key (the ADR explicitly says: 'where a long-lived signing key lives and who can use it is a custody decision with consequences that outlive any release'). No signing key is checked into this clone and no environment variable is set, by design.
entries.reason: Signing-key custody is a human-owned decision (see `docs/adr/ADR-RELEASE-PROVENANCE-PIPELINEK.md`, the 'Open decision' section). The script itself refuses to mint a key, and the lane does not have one to pass. SKIP_NOT_APPLICABLE rather than NOT_RUN because the script's behaviour on this environment is the same as the script's behaviour on any environment without a key: it returns exit 1 with the documented 'no signing key given (--key)' error. The lane runs the script as part of the release pipeline, where the key is provided by the release operator; that run will produce a bundle whose subject digest is re-checked against the artefact's sha256 (see attest-provenance.sh lines 224-235).

entries.result: `cosign` is on PATH (exit 0). The signer the attest script depends on is installed and invokable. The script's `command -v cosign >/dev/null 2>&1` check would pass.
entries.reason: Closing the dependency-on-PATH claim on the actual observation. If cosign were missing, CP4-01's --help path would still pass (the cosign check is gated behind argument parsing), but CP4-02 (real attestation) would fail at runtime; the gate moves CP4-02 from SKIP_NOT_APPLICABLE to FAIL at the same point.

entries.result: validate-mode output: `workspace.version=0.101.15` followed by `OK: validate-mode expected.version 0.101.15 ↔ workspace.version 0.101.15`. The script reads `Cargo.toml` from the blob at SHA e51f49ef without checking it out, parses `[workspace.package].version`, and confirms the requested version (0.101.15) matches the workspace version (0.101.15).
entries.reason: Closing the workspace-version coherence claim on the observed exit 0 + `OK: validate-mode` line. The version 0.101.15 is the workspace version at HEAD; it is the version that the v0.101.16 bump will replace (the bump itself is a separate release commit and not part of this cert).

entries.result: no v0.101.16 tag exists yet (the most recent annotated tag is v0.101.15 at commit 79600316, which is four commits behind HEAD e51f49ef). The tag-coherence identity check (tag resolves to the same commit as the build SHA) cannot run until the v0.101.16 tag is cut.
entries.reason: v0.101.16 has not been tagged. The release-lane stage that cuts the tag runs immediately after the version bump commit lands; this cert will be regenerated in the same release cycle that produces v0.101.16, and CP5-02 will move from NOT_RUN to PASS at the tag's commit SHA.

entries.result: no v0.101.16 SHA256SUMS on disk; the only SHA256SUMS in `release/` is the one for v0.101.10. A three-digest check (candidate digest == attestation subject digest == published digest) requires all three to exist; only the artefact side is missing because the v0.101.16 release has not been cut.
entries.reason: SHA256SUMS is generated by the release-pipeline stage that runs immediately before publishing. No v0.101.16 SHA256SUMS has been generated; the check is recorded as NOT_RUN with the precise missing artefact named, so a reviewer can verify the gap is real and not an oversight.

entries.result: no v0.101.16 release inventory on disk; the only inventory in `release/` is `release-inventory-0.101.10.json`. The release inventory records per-artifact SHA256, size, platform, installable flag, and profiles; a v0.101.16 inventory will be generated by the same release-pipeline stage that produces the artefacts.
entries.reason: Same root cause as CP5-03: the inventory is generated by the release-pipeline stage that has not run for v0.101.16. Recording as NOT_RUN rather than FAIL because the missing artefact is the gap, not a regression.

out_of_scope: CP6 (web / landing) — explicitly excluded by the B6.W5 scope per `docs/roadmap/2026-Q4-CLI-MCP-ROADMAP.md` (BLOQUE B6).
musl / macOS / Windows distribution — declared `unsupported` or `experimental` in `product/platforms.json`; not certified per PRF-DIST-05.
Linux aarch64 certification — the cross-build lane exists but no native aarch64 runner was exercised in this environment, so the cross-built artefact is not promoted to certified.
notes: Every NOT_RUN / SKIP_NOT_APPLICABLE entry has a `reason` field. The companion test suite `crates/cognicode-core/tests/b6_w5_distribution_certification.rs` enforces this with two named tests (`no_silent_skips` and `no_unjustified_not_run`) so a future commit cannot quietly remove a justification.

No `FAIL` entry is recorded. A FAIL would mean a script that exists and is supposed to run on this clone returned non-zero; no such incident is present. If one were observed, the cert would move it from PASS to FAIL with the exit code and a captured stdout/stderr snippet.

The cert entry `head_sha` and the workspace `cp5_workspace_version` are checkable: the companion test `cp5_workspace_version_consistent` reads both and asserts equality. A stale cert (regenerated against a different SHA or a different workspace version) fails the contract.
